texts.preamble: Ashok Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 9 May, 2025 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ? Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:75507 Court No. - 64 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2673 of 2011 Revisionist :- Ashok Kumar Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr. Counsel for Revisionist :- J.N. Gupta,Pradyumna Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: 5. The facts of the case are that on 31.05.1997 at about 2 pm C.R. Sharma the Food Inspector suspecting besan to be adulterated took its sample from the shop of the revisionist where it was kept for sale and sent it for analysis to the public analyst. The same was analysed in which the public analyst through its report dated 30.06.1997 reported it to be containing Khesari Dal which was prohibited item. Proceedings were then undertaken and sanction of the C.M.O., Allhabad was taken after which notice under Section 13 (2) of the Act of 1954 was sent to the revisionist on 21.04.1999. 6. A complaint dated 20.04.1999 was filed before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2, Allahabad on 10.05.1999. The trial in the mater started in which C.R. Sharma examined as P.W.-1 and Sanjay Kumar Srivastava the Food Clerk was examined as P.W.-2. 7. The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution version and stated that no such sample was taken from his shop. The present revision has thus been filed before this Court.
texts.arguments: 10. Learned counsel for the revisionist has agitated single argument that the valuable right of the revisionist under Section 13 (2) of the Act has been defeated in as much as notice under Section 13 (2) of the Act has been sent to the revisionist on 21.04.1999 which is about 19 days prior to the filing of the present complaint which has been filed on 10.05.1999. It is submitted that as such the revisionist was not in the knowledge of the fact as to where he has to exercise his right or not and thus the said right gets defeated since the notice has been sent prior to the filing of the complaint. Learned counsel has relied upon the judgement of this Court in the case of Muzaffar Vs. State of U.P.:1987 ACC 25 to buttress the said argument. It is submitted that since the right under Section 13 (2) of the Food Adulteration Act has been defeated, the present revision deserves to be allowed. Ashok Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8923231/ 2 11. Learned counsel for the State although opposed the revision and argument but could not dispute the factual aspect of the matter.
